name: Termux
insteadOf: Hauling out a laptop whenever you need a real shell
hook: A full Linux terminal environment on your phone — over 1,000 packages including git, Python, Node.js, and OpenSSH, with no root required.
bullets: Install real packages with pkg/apt: git, python, nodejs, vim, nmap, and more
No root — a complete Linux userland runs inside the app sandbox
SSH client and server, so your phone can reach or host remote machines
Termux:API bridges the shell to device hardware: SMS, camera, sensors
benefits: A genuine command-line environment — not a toy shell with five commands
Automate your phone, run a dev server, or SSH into your machines from anywhere
Scripting and tooling behave like a familiar Linux box
Free, open source, and the de facto standard terminal on Android
setupSteps: Install Termux from F-Droid or GitHub releases — never the Play Store build
Run pkg update && pkg upgrade to refresh the package repos
Install what you need: pkg install git python openssh …
Run termux-setup-storage to share files with the rest of Android
details: Termux is an Android terminal emulator with its own Linux userland: it ships a package manager (pkg/apt) with over 1,000 installable packages, so git, Python, Node.js, Rust, vim, tmux, openssh, nmap, and the rest of a normal toolkit run natively — without root, in a sandboxed app. Add Termux:API and the shell can read SMS, place calls, trigger the camera, and query sensors, which makes it a legitimate automation hub. It is also a competent remote machine: run an SSH client to reach your servers, or an sshd to let them reach your phone. The one rule the project insists on: install from F-Droid or the project's GitHub releases, because the Play Store build is an outdated, Google-signed version that no longer receives updates, and the two signatures are incompatible — do not mix APKs between channels. GPL-3.0 (with Apache-2.0 exceptions for the embedded terminal-emulator libraries).
setup: App (Android) — install from F-Droid, then pkg install
